accuracy.evidence: Matches the Year 6 statutory requirement to use passive verbs to affect the presentation of information, and the Appendix 2 example (The window in the greenhouse was broken (by me)). Every passive was checked for be + past participle and agreement: was broken, are cooked, was made, was blown, are chosen, are marked. Look-alikes were checked against the glossary: was delicious and were happy are be + adjective, was running is the past progressive.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips teachers report in Year 6 and KS3 writing: the simple past for the participle (was broke, was blew, was make tiles and challenge), any sentence with was counted as passive (cake, Tom was running, were happy, door was green), the first noun taken as the doer (the cat prediction, the song option), number agreement with the new subject (is cooked tile, tests is marked), and the belief that passive is always better or shorter.

lab_distinct.evidence: The flagvoice lab is built around the voice transformation itself: learners locate the agent in active and passive word rows, assemble receiver / be + participle / by + agent chunks into three labelled slots, sort real passives from be + adjective and progressive look-alikes, decide whether a by-phrase earns its place, and pick a voice for three writing purposes. Highest shingle overlap with any other lab is 5.8% (flag_contr.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: The order moves from noticing to making to judging: first who does the action whatever the word order, then the three-part passive pattern with a wrong participle or wrong agreement as the decoy, then the test that separates passives from look-alikes, then the optional agent, then purpose. Each finished task states the rule just discovered, for example that be must agree with the new subject.

predictions.evidence: Three committed guesses come before the evidence: who did the chasing in The cat was chased by the dog (tempting: the cat, because it comes first), what happens to broke in the passive (tempting: it stays as was broke), and whether The cake was delicious is passive (tempting: yes, because it has was). Each done message reveals the locked answer against what the task just showed.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with its own reply: act explains the doer is still the subject, ing names the past progressive, past names blew versus blown, first says word order does not make a doer, gone points to the by-phrase, always and short correct the style myths, pp explains which door sentence is passive, agree and swap name agreement and meaning change.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs score Flesch-Kincaid grade 2.3 with one new term per paragraph (doer, receiver, passive voice, past participle) shown in a worked sentence; adult text was rewritten into short sentences and now scores 5.7, under the learner limit of 9.5, while still naming agent, by-phrase and agentless passive. Lab prompts stay to one short instruction.

no_filler.evidence: The key idea gives the definition, the be + past participle pattern and both reasons to use the passive in five sentences. The family tip is a single headline activity. Adult notes cover the Year 6 statement, how the passive is formed, five named mistakes and what each lab step does. Every practice item tests one voice fact; numeric items count passives, agentless passives or active sentences.

mobile.evidence: Walked through on an iPhone 13 viewport and desktop with all six steps, five tasks completed through Show me and the challenge shown. On the phone the chunk tiles sit in a two by two grid above three dashed slots, the six sentence cards wrap into two columns, and the keep/cut cards sit side by side with both versions of the sentence printed inside; nothing was clipped in the screenshots.

accessibility.evidence: axe reported no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme on desktop or phone. Every canvas action has a button twin below the canvas (one per word, chunk, sentence card, Keep it / Cut it, and both voice versions), the canvas aria-label mirrors every spoken status, and challenge feedback uses a polite live region.
